rationale: GPT-6-luna is the only unevaluated lever — $0.10/$0.50 per 1M tokens, half the cost of GPT-5-6-luna, suggesting a smaller/faster model class. The frontier is tight (quality best 0.95, latency best 25772ms, epsilons 0.03 / 2000ms): Round 2's +0.025 quality gain on GPT-5-6-luna was reverted for falling short of the 0.03 quality epsilon, so the only remaining single-step attack vector is latency. If GPT-6-luna's median comes in meaningfully below Haiku's 25772ms (expected from a smaller model in the same luna family that GPT-5-6-luna sits in), we extend the latency frontier past the 2000ms epsilon. The quality guard is forgiving: Haiku lost only 0.025 vs Sonnet and Round 2 showed GPT-5-6-luna matched Sonnet-class quality on FINRA PDFs, so GPT-6-luna has a plausible chance of staying inside the 0.03 quality tolerance (summary ≥0.84, i.e. ≥17/20 passes). Single-step mutation = crisp attribution: if quality holds and latency drops, we win; if quality regresses >0.03 we revert cleanly and round 4 can compound a Haiku fallback for complex rules (e.g., finra_2360 Options). This probe closes the lever matrix before any code-level complexity is justified.
